Produce verified change requests and a ranked repair recommendation that gives the L1 validation and build runtime exactly one governed owner without weakening evidence, public-private, or authority boundaries.

groups.anti_bias: methodology. Predicted disagreements: van Lamsweerde runs formal obligation traceability and Hewitt runs empirical runtime reuse on the methodology axis; a bias in van Lamsweerde toward inventing a new formal owner would be exposed by Hewitt's live reuse proof, while a bias in Hewitt toward executable sufficiency would be exposed by van Lamsweerde's unowned-obligation trace. van Lamsweerde runs formal contract completeness and Bateson runs adversarial lifecycle pressure on the methodology axis; a bias in van Lamsweerde toward accepting a named contract would be exposed by Bateson's hidden-side-effect attack, while a bias in Bateson toward rejecting all shared seams would be exposed by van Lamsweerde's exact owner trace. Hewitt runs executable runtime counterexamples and Bateson runs adversarial boundary analysis on the methodology axis; a bias in Hewitt toward one successful run would be exposed by Bateson's pin, cache, cleanup, and receipt attack, while a bias in Bateson toward textual rejection would be exposed by Hewitt's isolated current-byte counterexample.
